svg.text: NeoBox exploded view — eight steps, three studs, and nothing glued
NeoBox is a flash light source box for camera-scanning (DSLR scanning) 35 mm and 120 film; the camera looks down on the film from above.
Front elevation, parts separated along the build axis in assembly order; the main body is cut open. True horizontal scale — the vertical gaps are exploded, and the 0.14 mm film is drawn thickened.

Assembly order — what each step does, and what holds it in place
Main body
One printed piece — floor 4, walls 3, cavity 202 × 267 × 88. The outside is sprayed matte
black; the inside stays bare white filament, because that is the light source.
Flash and trigger receiver
Lies flat, head turned 90° so it fires at the far wall. Receiver at its foot, white paper taped
to its top face. Nothing holds it down — it goes in last, through the access opening.
Top cover
Drops on. The 10 mm skirt laps the wall, locates the cover and traps light. No screws.
Three M6 heat-set inserts sit in the posts underneath.
Three M6 × 35 studs, six nuts
Screwed into the inserts. The lower nut sets the stage height, the upper nut clamps it.
Front stud (45, −100) is pitch; the rear pair (±70, +65) is roll.
Film stage
200 × 230, a 5 mm plate with integral corner L-blocks rising to 11 mm. Aperture 100 ×
120. Three Ø6.5 clearance holes — never tap them. Top face at z = 114.
Opal diffuser
110 × 130 × 2 opal acrylic, laid over the aperture. No fixings: the weight of the holder
keeps it flat, 4.3 mm below the film.
Film holder — base, film, lid
Base and lid both 110 × 170, located in X and Y by the four corner blocks. The film slides
in sideways; the holder is never opened mid-roll. Film plane z ≈ 120.3.
Closure magnets
Four Ø6 × 2 pairs at (±45, ±75) clamp the sandwich shut — 8 per holder. Four more base
magnets and Ø12 steel washers only if you will stand the box on end.
How each interface is held
Screw-clamped
An M6 stud in an insert, or a nut on a stud. Holds in any orientation.
Magnetic
Ø6 × 2 neodymium pairs. Stays shut with the box on end; opens with your fingers.
Resting under gravity
Located by geometry, held by its own weight. Lift it straight off.
Nothing in the enclosure is glued or screwed together.
The cover drops on, the diffuser and the holder just sit there, and the only fasteners in the whole box are
three M6 studs and six nuts. The only adhesive anywhere in the build is one drop of cyanoacrylate under
each magnet and each steel washer.

Every dimension comes from cad/neobox.blend. Assembly order, interfaces and fastening methods follow docs/assembly.md. The 135 holder is drawn; the 120 holder shares the same 110 × 170 outline. The access panel (200
× 78 × 16) closes a 190 × 76 opening in the front wall — the wall this section removes — so neither is drawn here; see manufacturing-overview.svg.
